description: Batch 6: scored every BigQuery gold (expect high) and every planted bug (expect low) in static mode with question text + params, and redid the 224-candidate false-alarm rate with REAL gold labels. Dev gold from holdout w4/w4v/w4v2/w5 (released/dev; held-out w5v/w6/w6v/w7 were NOT fetched).

part1_false_alarm_rate_real_gold.note: stricter than the batch-5 native-consensus proxy (126); correctness = candidate native == gold native on all of clean-1/nasty-42/nasty-44
part1_false_alarm_rate_real_gold.case: hr_snapshot-q027 (gemma-3-27b), required_predicate HIGH on the IN-subquery hierarchy scope (batch-5 finding), now scored 0.087 with question text

part2_gold_scores.native_only_note: w5 control-flow scripts (DECLARE + IF/SET/END IF) are bigquery_(script_)native_only; sqlgami correctly declines to bind them (kind=multiple), scoring ~0.05 -- not a false alarm, consistent with batch-3 'binder does not pretend'.
part2_gold_scores.ceiling_note: NO gold reaches 'confident' (max 0.588). Correct answers are capped in the 0.50-0.59 band by ubiquitous partition_filter (LOW) and recurring scalar_subquery_rows / top_n / limit_without_order (MEDIUM).

part2_bug_catch_rate.note: static mode has no execution, so value bugs that produce valid SQL with wrong numbers cannot be caught statically -- they need the fixtures/translation stage. Structural/predicate bugs are caught.

misses_by_class.missing_required_predicate: 1/1 missed (b038 -- a glossary hire_dt-in-window predicate, not the hierarchy check; a semantic/term bug)
misses_by_class.array_agg_wrong_order: 1/1 missed (ordering inside ARRAY_AGG; value-level, needs execution)

findings.symptom: the or_chain hierarchy matcher does not recognize an UNNEST-pivot scope (explode the 12 level columns into one node_id via UNNEST([STRUCT(...)]) and filter node_id = manager); a correct gold is flagged HIGH. Together with the IN-subquery form (batch 5, q027) the matcher misses multiple idiomatic scopings, including the owner's own gold.
findings.minimal_construct: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT eps.assoc_id) FROM emp_period_snapshot eps, UNNEST([STRUCT(eps.lvl_2_id AS node_id), ... all 12 ...]) x WHERE eps.status_cd='A' AND x.node_id = 12003

findings.symptom: term_rank reports 'the query uses a plain row limit' and fires HIGH on a correct top-N that uses QUALIFY DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY active_n DESC) <= 3 -- solely because of an unrelated LIMIT 1 inside a current-period scalar subquery (period_end_dt = (SELECT ppe_dt ... is_current_flag LIMIT 1)). Removing that incidental LIMIT 1 clears the HIGH.
findings.minimal_construct: a top-N with QUALIFY DENSE_RANK() <= 3 whose scope includes period_end_dt = (SELECT ppe_dt ... LIMIT 1); the DENSE_RANK top-N is correct, the LIMIT 1 is incidental
